```text
Create a new SystemVerilog IP block for the FPGA Cores 4 U digital IP library.
```

## 1. Identity

- Module name: `coord_gen`

- One-line purpose: Reusable IP. Per-pixel source-address generator.
- Version: 1.0.0

## 2. Context

- Where it is used: `video_processor`, `vision_system`.
- Existing IP to reuse (do not duplicate):

| Module | From | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `barrel_pkg` | `vision_system` | Shared SystemVerilog package for the lens-distortion- correction core. |
| `distortion_model_pkg` | `vision_system` | Defines distortion_model_e (the MODEL_SEL enum: radial, fisheye, affine, perspective, scaling, panoramic) and calib_params_t, the single packed struct bundling every camera-calibration and distortion  |
| `fixed_recip` | `fixed_recip` | Reusable IP. Iterative shift/subtract unsigned Q16.16 reciprocal divider (33 cycles). |
| `mulq_s` | `mulq` | Reusable IP. Timing-friendly signed 32x32 multiply with the Q16.16 shift built in: s = (a*b) >>> 16 as an exact 48-bit signed value, in 2 cycles. |

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Reusable IP. Per-pixel source-address generator. Fast
23-cycle path for radial/tangential distortion and the
affine/scaling hooks; a second "slow path" per-pixel divide
FSM (reusing fixed_recip) implements fisheye, panoramic, and
perspective correction. All multiplies use the mulq_s IP.
=============================================================================
coord_gen.sv

For each output (corrected-image) pixel (x,y), computes the fractional
source coordinate to sample from the (distorted) input frame. Camera-
calibration-style pinhole normalization, then (when cfg.model_sel ==
distortion_model_pkg::MODEL_RADIAL) the standard radial+tangential ("plumb bob") distortion
model:

nx = (x - cx_pix) / fx_pix          -- normalize (pinhole intrinsics)
ny = (y - cy_pix) / fy_pix
r2 = nx^2 + ny^2
radial   = 1 + k1*r2 + k2*r2^2 + k3*r2^3        (k3 * r^6 term)
tang_x   = 2*p1*nx*ny + p2*(r2 + 2*nx^2)
tang_y   =   p1*(r2 + 2*ny^2) + 2*p2*nx*ny
sx = cx_pix + (nx*radial + tang_x) * fx_pix
sy = cy_pix + (ny*radial + tang_y) * fy_pix

cfg (calib_params_t, distortion_model_pkg.sv) bundles every one of the
above parameters into a single struct port -- see that package for why.

ARCHITECTURE HOOK: when cfg.model_sel != distortion_model_pkg::MODEL_RADIAL (i.e. one of the
reserved FISHEYE/AFFINE/PERSPECTIVE/SCALING/PANORAMIC slots), the k1/k2/k3/p1/p2
contributions are gated to zero right where they're computed (stage 5
below) rather than being threaded through extra "is this the active
model" muxing at every later stage -- radial=1.0, tangential=0 falls
straight out of the existing math with no separate identity datapath,
so this reduces to the same normalize/denormalize round-trip the
current pinhole intrinsics already define (matches the golden models'
identity-passthrough for these model IDs bit-for-bit -- see the
project's smoke test). Implementing an actual FISHEYE/AFFINE/
PERSPECTIVE/SCALING projection means replacing this gate with real
per-model math -- see README.md "Extension hooks" for the equations
and where each would plug in.

All arithmetic is Q16.16 (see barrel_pkg). This is a fully pipelined,
feed-forward (no feedback/stall) datapath: one (x,y) request may be
accepted every clock cycle, with a fixed LATENCY-cycle delay to the
corresponding output (LATENCY=23 since the timing work: every multiply
goes through the mulq_s IP -- it was 9 with one single-cycle qmul per
stage. Confirmed by direct measurement -- see the latency-probe
methodology described in README.md).

TIMING: an earlier revision of this comment claimed the design "easily
meets 100 MHz (single 32x32 multiply per stage)". That was wrong: a
one-cycle 32x32 multiply plus its shift/saturate/add is ~11 ns of
logic on 7-series, and the slow path chained five of them. Measured
with synth/est_timing.py the worst path was ~48 ns. After the timing
work it is ~6.5 ns in this module (~7.2 ns in mulq_s) -- see README.
=============================================================================
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - coord_gen (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] OpenCV, Camera Calibration and 3D Reconstruction (calib3d): x'' = x'(1 + k1 r^2 + k2
//   r^4 + k3 r^6) + 2 p1 x'y' + p2 (r^2 + 2x'^2), y'' = y'(...) + p1 (r^2 + 2y'^2) + 2 p2 x'y',
//   u = fx x'' + cx, https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d9/d0c/group__calib3d.html; fisheye: theta =
//   atan(r), theta_d = theta (1 + k1 theta^2 + k2 theta^4 + k3 theta^6 + k4 theta^8),
//   https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/db/d58/group__calib3d__fisheye.html
//   [2] A. W. Fitzgibbon, "Simultaneous linear estimation of multiple view geometry and lens
//   distortion", CVPR 2001, doi:10.1109/CVPR.2001.990465 (division model r_u = r_d / (1 + k
//   r_d^2))
//   [3] R. Hartley, A. Zisserman, "Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision", 2nd ed.,
//   Cambridge 2004, ch. 2 / 4 (planar homography x' = H x, h33 = 1 normalisation)
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   OpenCV plumb-bob model: x' = (u - cx) / fx, r^2 = x'^2 + y'^2, x'' = x'(1 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4
//   + k3 r^6) + 2 p1 x'y' + p2 (r^2 + 2x'^2), y'' = y'(...) + p1 (r^2 + 2y'^2) + 2 p2 x'y',
//   u_src = fx x'' + cx. Fisheye (OpenCV): theta = atan(r), theta_d = theta(1 + k1 theta^2 + k2
//   theta^4 + k3 theta^6 + k4 theta^8). Division model (Fitzgibbon 2001): r_u = r_d / (1 + k
//   r_d^2). Homography (Hartley & Zisserman): x' = (h11 x + h12 y + h13) / (h31 x + h32 y + 1).
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Radial / tangential path matches OpenCV term for term (k1, k2, k3, p1, p2, pinhole
//   normalisation). Perspective matches the h33 = 1 homography. Differs: MODEL_FISHEYE /
//   MODEL_PANORAMIC use the division model, not OpenCV's equidistant theta polynomial, so
//   coefficients from cv::fisheye::calibrate cannot be used directly; MODEL_AFFINE /
//   MODEL_SCALING are reserved hooks (identity).
// TODO(REF-COORD_GEN-1) [MEDIUM] Fisheye model. Prompt: in
//   image_processing/vision_system/ip/coord_gen/src/coord_gen.sv, state in the header that
//   MODEL_FISHEYE is Fitzgibbon's division model (CVPR 2001) and not the OpenCV fisheye
//   (Kannala-Brandt) model, and give the conversion used by the calibration software;
//   optionally add MODEL_FISHEYE_KB computing theta = atan(r) with a CORDIC or LUT and theta_d
//   = theta(1 + k1 theta^2 + k2 theta^4 + k3 theta^6 + k4 theta^8), with a golden-model test
//   against cv::fisheye::distortPoints values.
// TODO(REF-COORD_GEN-2) [LOW] Reserved models. Prompt: in coord_gen.sv and
//   distortion_model_pkg.sv, either implement MODEL_AFFINE (sx = a11 x + a12 y + a13, sy = a21
//   x + a22 y + a23) and MODEL_SCALING, or make the register block reject those MODEL_SEL
//   values (SLVERR) so software cannot select an identity mapping by mistake.
```


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: report the Yosys utilisation; keep it in line with similar library blocks.

## 8. File header

Read the file header template from `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt` and start every file you create (RTL, testbench, test tasks, scripts, file lists, Makefile) with that header, filled in: Filename, Author: FPGA Cores 4 U, Description, Date. In RTL the Description is the specification (behaviour, register map, parameters, clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings, latency, resources, errors); in testbenches it says what is checked; test-task files list every task with a one-line description (the test list scripts use it).

Header template file: `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt`   (replace with your own template file if needed)

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking standalone testbench for coord_gen, with
its own inline golden reference. Covers identity, radial,
tangential, camera calibration, real fisheye/panoramic/
perspective math, remaining hooks, and large-frame boundary
coordinates (479/719).
The test tasks are in tests/coord_gen_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `the simulation script --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `tb_coord_gen` | `tb_coord_gen` | one test: Self-checking standalone testbench for coord_gen, with its own inline golden reference. |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: the block's `scripts/run.sh` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, synthesis passes.
